Verbatim verdict preserved in control-plane/verdicts/acp001-codex-verdict-31951393592.json (immutable artifact acp001-codex-verdict-31951393592, artifact id 9264790890, zip sha256 4641d64b382e1bc83ef243fb4aa125ba46521172305b62907788a6075f000194, retained by GitHub only until 2026-09-15, therefore committed here).

Verdict preconditions verified before any transition: audited_sha == 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539 (the exact frozen candidate), independent == true, read_only == true, verdict within {PASS, FAIL, UNVERIFIABLE}. The judge workflow enforced the same four conditions in-run via jq before persisting the artifact.

All twelve mandatory gates returned PASS: schema_validation, single_active_program, single_active_writer, deterministic_selection, transition_table, owner_policy_invariants, writer_lock, unverifiable_not_pass, p2_p3_no_auto_repair, legacy_authority_rejected, reverse_mutation_proof, focused_tests. findings == [] — no P0, no blocking P1, and no non-blocking P2/P3 was raised.

Audit integrity proved by the run itself: the judge checked out the frozen candidate with persist-credentials:false, asserted HEAD == 907447a2 with an empty worktree before auditing, and proved orchestration_head_at_start == orchestration_head_at_end == 8def4b841771a98955ff08aa36fbaf8f80e41003, so SHA_CHANGED_DURING_AUDIT did not occur.

Transition recorded: RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_PASS. Proved legal by the kernel itself under the real verdict context — evaluateTransition('RUNNING_JUDGE','JUDGE_PASS',{judge_verdict:'PASS',judge_independent:true,judge_read_only:true}) returns ok=true, and statusForJudgeVerdict('PASS') independently maps the verdict to JUDGE_PASS.

Transition recorded: JUDGE_PASS -> CLOSED. evaluateTransition('JUDGE_PASS','CLOSED', same context) returns ok=true; guardClosureRequiresIndependentJudge accepted it only because verdict==PASS, judge_independent==true and judge_read_only==true were all present.

No state was skipped: evaluateTransition('RUNNING_JUDGE','CLOSED', same context) is rejected with SKIPPED_STATE ('skips 1 required state(s)'), so closure could not have been reached without passing through JUDGE_PASS. The board therefore travelled READY -> RUNNING_WRITER -> WRITER_DONE -> CI_PENDING -> SHA_FROZEN -> RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_FAIL -> REPAIR_READY -> RUNNING_WRITER -> WRITER_DONE -> CI_PENDING -> SHA_FROZEN -> RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_PASS -> CLOSED with every edge in the transition table.

Required CI for the audited artefact is CI #1018 run 31924253766 on the exact frozen SHA 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539: SUCCESS across all five jobs. The closure commit does not alter control-plane/kernel.mjs, control-plane/MASTER_BOARD.schema.json, or any product, clinical or deployment file, so the audited BEHAVIOUR is byte-identical to what Codex judged.

P3 (non-blocking, found while closing, not present in the Codex findings): the focused-test fixture `readyBoard()` was value-coupled to live board state. It rewound ACP-001 to READY without rewinding the items that depend on ACP-001, so the first legal advance past ACP-001 made the fixture itself incoherent and the kernel correctly rejected it with BLOCKED_BY_OUT_OF_SYNC. The kernel was right and the fixture was wrong; the two failing cases were 'happy path: exactly one eligible item is selected deterministically' and 'happy path: an in-flight item is advanced, never replaced by a second writer'. Fixed forward inside control-plane/kernel.test.mjs by making the rewind generic — every item after ACP-001 returns to QUEUED with a truthful blocker list. No guard, no assertion and no expected violation code was changed, added or relaxed; the suite still holds 67 cases. Per the execution policy a P3 does not open a repair loop, so this is recorded as evidence rather than escalated.

The fixture fix also restored a proof that had gone vacuous: 'dependency violation: blocked_by must tell the truth about open dependencies' sets ACP-002's blockers to [], which is only a real mutation while the fixture actually declares ACP-001 as a blocker.

Closure verification re-run on the closing tree: node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs -> 67 pass, 0 fail; node control-plane/kernel.mjs check -> ok=true, violation_count=0, exit code 0. Reverse-proved: the pre-fix fixture against the post-closure board fails 2 of 67, so the fixture change is load-bearing and not cosmetic.
No forbidden action was taken to close: no merge, no deploy, no PHI, no destructive change, no clinical-policy change, no secret rotation, no product or clinical code touched.

items.title: Cloud writer runner
items.next_action: Checkpointed bounded repair of the seven blocking P1s from Codex run 31963800078 is in progress. Claude/Opus is the single writer; completed chunks are persisted before the next chunk.
evidence: Unblocked by the closure of ACP-001 on independent Codex PASS (run 31951393592, frozen SHA 907447a20c93c60483e1e6a0156e49964cd7e539). The dependency is met, so `blocked_by` may no longer name ACP-001 — the kernel rejects a closed item left standing as a blocker (BLOCKED_BY_OUT_OF_SYNC).

FROZEN_ORCHESTRATION_SHA=8cda1aac5c59749e2196f7fbde6eed1334c8f067 — the immutable post-closure orchestration state ACP-002 starts from. At that SHA ACP-001 is CLOSED with its closer recorded, the board validates with zero violations, and the focused suite is 67/67.

Transition recorded: QUEUED -> READY. evaluateTransition('QUEUED','READY') returns ok=true, and the unblocking is real rather than declared: ACP-001 is CLOSED, so ACP-002's dependency is met and its blocker list is legitimately empty.

Transition recorded: READY -> RUNNING_WRITER. acquireWriterLock(NO_LOCK,{item_id:'ACP-002',holder:'CLAUDE_OPUS',run_id:'session_015nBJM7SgZNm63MtpxVNsVg'}) granted the lock, and evaluateTransition('READY','RUNNING_WRITER',{item_id:'ACP-002',writer_lock:<granted>}) returns ok=true. The same call without the lock is refused with WRITER_LOCK_NOT_HELD, and a second run claiming the held lock is refused with WRITER_LOCK_HELD — so the single-writer rule is enforced, not merely asserted.
One active writer, one active program: ACP-002 is the only item in an in-flight status, and the board's own concurrency check would report MULTIPLE_IN_FLIGHT_ITEMS if that stopped being true.

DELIVERABLE 1 — control-plane/preflight.mjs: the fourteen BASELINE.md preflight conditions as deterministic, dependency-free code with one machine-readable answer and one exact stop condition. BASELINE.md §'Required fail-closed bootstrap preflight' lists fourteen bullets, not thirteen; the earlier note in this item miscounted them and is corrected here. Every condition is evaluated on every run, so one run reports everything that is wrong instead of one thing at a time, and any failure sets next_board_status=BLOCKED with authorized=null.

Conditions 10 and 12-14 are proved by INTERROGATING THE KERNEL at run time, not by restating its rules: the preflight actually calls evaluateTransition with the exact defect and requires the exact rejection. A preflight that merely re-asserted 'UNVERIFIABLE is never PASS' in a second file would stay green while the kernel underneath it was weakened.

DELIVERABLE 2 — .github/workflows/control-plane-writer.yml: workflow_dispatch only (nothing auto-fires a writer), concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:false, timeout 60 min, and permissions contents:write with pull-requests, issues, actions, deployments, id-token and packages all explicitly none. It replaces the ACP-001 bootstrap's hardcoded commit-subject modes with the board's own deterministic selection, refuses to write any item other than the one the preflight authorized, enforces a control-plane/** path allowlist, re-runs the focused suite before pushing, and pushes only to the branch the board declares.

The runner cannot deploy to production and cannot merge to main: it holds no deployment, environment or id-token scope, and both the preflight (condition 4) and the push step refuse main/master and any branch other than board.source_branch.

The runner cannot widen its own privileges: .github/** is deliberately absent from the writer's path allowlist, so a writer cannot edit the workflow that grants its token. A test asserts that absence rather than trusting the comment.

El dato tiene que LLEGAR: the permissions handed to the preflight are PARSED OUT OF THE WORKFLOW FILE the runner runs under (writerPermissionsFromWorkflow), not typed a second time. Two hand-maintained copies of a permission list drift, and the copy that drifts is always the one being checked. A test reads the real committed workflow, extracts its real block, and proves the preflight authorizes exactly it — plus a reverse proof that widening deployments to write is caught. The parser throws on any shape it does not understand, because an empty permission list reads as harmless and is the one answer it must never produce by accident.

Tests: control-plane/preflight.test.mjs, 54 focused cases. Direct negative case and reverse/mutation proof for conditions 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9; kernel-mutation proofs for 10, 12, 13 and 14 in which the KERNEL is weakened and the preflight is required to notice. Full control-plane suite: 121 pass, 0 fail (67 kernel + 54 preflight); no existing test was deleted, relaxed or renamed.

Two defects were found by these tests during the writing of them, both in the new code, both fixed: (a) a request declaring permissions {contents:write, deployments:none} was rejected as 'unanticipated scope' because a disclaimed production scope fell through to the allowlist — explicitly disclaiming a production scope is good practice, not a fault; (b) the writer lock used a sentinel run_id ('__unknown_run__') to stand in for the unknown holder, so a request that simply CLAIMED to be the sentinel was treated as the holder. A guessable secret is not a lock. An active lock is now refused outright, because the board records that a writer is running but never which run is running it.

Recorded, not repaired: the UNVERIFIABLE property survives removal of either guardUnverifiableNeverPasses or guardJudgePassRequiresVerdict alone, because the ACP-001 repair left two layers behind it. That is defence in depth working as intended; the test now asserts it explicitly and only demands a writer halt when BOTH layers are gone, so the proof cannot be satisfied by a coincidence.

Verification on this checkpoint: node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs -> 121 pass, 0 fail; node control-plane/kernel.mjs check -> ok=true, violation_count=0; the workflow parses as valid YAML; and the preflight CLI was dry-run against the live board, correctly refusing with ITEM_NOT_AUTHORIZED and failed conditions [2,3] because ACP-002 is itself RUNNING_WRITER — the fail-closed path exercised on real state, not a fixture.

Scope honoured: only control-plane/** and the one new workflow file changed. No product, clinical or deployment code was touched; no dependency was added; the ACP-001 kernel and schema are byte-identical to the SHA Codex judged. No merge, no deploy, no PHI, no destructive change, no clinical-policy change, no secret rotation, and no credential value was read, printed or stored.

Transition recorded: RUNNING_WRITER -> WRITER_DONE. evaluateTransition('RUNNING_WRITER','WRITER_DONE') returns ok=true. JUDGE_PASS and CLOSED remain unclaimed: ACP-002 closure requires required CI on a frozen SHA and one independent read-only Codex audit, exactly as ACP-001 did. The writer also cannot close itself — WRITER_DONE -> CLOSED is rejected with SKIPPED_STATE ('skips 2 required state(s)').

Repository gates run locally on this exact working tree, all five commands the CI jobs run: npx vitest run -> 9692 pass, 1 skipped, 1 failed; npx tsc --noEmit -> exit 0; npm run build (with the CI placeholder Firebase env) -> exit 0; node scripts/lint-trinquete.mjs -> 96 errors, equal to the ceiling, no new debt; node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs -> 121 pass.

The one vitest failure is diagnosed, not dismissed: src/__tests__/la-agenda-es-un-riel.test.ts timed out at 5000ms on a dynamic import while the lint ratchet was running concurrently on the same container (that run reported import 362.15s in aggregate). Re-run alone it passes 12/12 in 4.35s with import 49ms. It touches src/app/(dashboard)/citas and has no relationship to control-plane/**. Recorded as resource contention with the evidence, not labelled flaky.

The local run above is superseded by the real cloud attestation: the owner authorized the pull request, and draft PR #295 (head claude/acp-001-codex-verdict-zwzvjk, base control-plane/autonomous-001) obtained it.

REQUIRED CI OBTAINED: CI run 31954336304 (run_number 1023, attempt 1, event pull_request) completed SUCCESS on the exact pushed SHA a0ab0a1b483e8ae1986f661db970560d265ed4b2. All five required jobs passed: clinical-safety 95182526960, verificar 95182526995, e2e-publico 95182527033, aislamiento-tenant 95182527046, lint (trinquete) 95182527088. The vitest timeout seen locally did not reproduce in CI, confirming it was container contention and not a defect.

No writer auto-fired when the PR opened: Control Plane Bootstrap run 31954336283 job 95182527502 concluded 'skipped', because its job guard requires head.ref == 'control-plane/autonomous-001'. One active writer was preserved without relying on anybody remembering not to push a magic commit subject.
Transition recorded: WRITER_DONE -> CI_PENDING after the exact writer SHA completed the required CI in GitHub Actions.

BLOCKER FOUND AGAINST THIS ITEM'S OWN DEFINITION OF DONE, and it is my own delivery: ACP-002 requires 'Run one bounded writer task in GitHub Actions', and the runner as delivered cannot be run there at all. It is workflow_dispatch-only, and GitHub only exposes workflow_dispatch for workflow files present on the DEFAULT branch. Verified, not assumed: POST /actions/workflows/control-plane-writer.yml/dispatches returns 404, the repository lists only three registered workflows (ci.yml, control-plane-bootstrap.yml, control-plane-acp001-judge.yml), and GET contents of .github/workflows/control-plane-writer.yml?ref=main returns 404. Getting it onto main is a merge to main, which is forbidden without explicit owner authorization.

CORRECTION to an earlier claim in this item's evidence: the ACP-001 bootstrap's pull_request trigger with commit-subject gating was described here as something this runner improves upon. The board-driven item selection is still the better design, but the trigger was not a mistake — a check of the same three facts shows control-plane-bootstrap.yml and control-plane-acp001-judge.yml are ALSO absent from main and have only ever run via pull_request. pull_request is the only trigger available to a control-plane workflow that has never reached the default branch. Choosing workflow_dispatch alone is what made this runner unattestable, and that is a defect in the new work, not in the old.

FAIL CLOSED: SHA_FROZEN is deliberately NOT taken. Freezing is the act that declares a candidate ready for the independent judge, and this candidate is known to be unable to satisfy the item's own attestation requirement. Handing it to Codex would spend a full audit cycle rediscovering a defect already found and written down. ACP-002 rests at CI_PENDING, whose legal successors remain SHA_FROZEN, CI_FAILED and BLOCKED, so no option is foreclosed.

Remedy identified but NOT applied, because it is new writer work on an item that has left the writer state and there is no legal WRITER_DONE/CI_PENDING -> RUNNING_WRITER edge: add a pull_request-triggered, read-only attestation job (permissions contents:read) to the writer workflow that runs preflight.mjs against real state and stops, never installing the Claude CLI and never pushing, while keeping workflow_dispatch for after the file reaches the default branch. Re-entering the writer state legally requires CI_PENDING -> BLOCKED -> OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED -> READY -> RUNNING_WRITER with recorded owner approval. That approval has not been given, so the transition has not been taken.
ACP-003 not started. No merge, no deploy, no PHI, no production credential, no clinical-policy change.

OWNER APPROVAL RECORDED: the owner reviewed the blocker above and authorized a bounded repair, strictly limited to making ACP-002 attestable on PR #295 before merge — a pull_request-triggered read-only attestation job with contents:read, running the committed control-plane/preflight.mjs against real PR state, with no Claude CLI, no push, no contents:write, no production credential, no deploy, no merge, no PHI, no product or clinical code, no widening of the workflow_dispatch writer permissions, and no ACP-003.
Transition recorded: CI_PENDING -> BLOCKED. The item was parked because its own definition of done could not be met, which is what BLOCKED is for.
Transition recorded: BLOCKED -> OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED. Legal without approval — the kernel lets a blocked item be escalated to the owner, it just will not let it leave on its own.

Transition recorded: OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED -> READY with owner_approval=true. The gate is real and was proved so at the moment of use: the same call without approval is refused with OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, BLOCKED -> READY is refused with SKIPPED_STATE, and CI_PENDING -> READY is refused with SKIPPED_STATE. There was no way to shortcut back into the writer state.

Transition recorded: READY -> RUNNING_WRITER, one writer, lock granted to run session_015nBJM7SgZNm63MtpxVNsVg-repair for ACP-002. Marked before the repair was written, so the lock is visible on the board while the writer works.

REPAIR DELIVERED, and only this: .github/workflows/control-plane-writer.yml gained a `pull_request` trigger and a second job, `attest`. Nothing else in the repository changed except this board and control-plane/preflight.test.mjs, which gained the tests that hold the repair in place. control-plane/preflight.mjs and control-plane/kernel.mjs were not touched.

The writer job is now gated with `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`. pull_request reaches this file, and it must never reach the writer; a test asserts the gate rather than trusting the comment.

The attest job holds `contents: read` and nothing else. It references no secret at all, so it cannot reach a provider even by accident, and there is nothing in it that could push. Tests assert: the attest block parses to exactly {contents:read}; the writer job's only write scope is still contents:write with every production-reaching scope still `none`; the two jobs' permission blocks are parsed separately with no bleed; and the attest half of the file contains no Claude CLI install, no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no git commit and no git push — with a counter-assertion that the writer half still does, so the check cannot pass against an empty slice.

What the attestation proves in GitHub Actions, without running a writer: (a) `node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs` and `node control-plane/kernel.mjs check` execute on the runner, so the harness is cloud-executable and does not depend on any local machine; (b) the committed writer permission block, parsed out of the workflow itself, is AUTHORIZED by the preflight; (c) eight deliberately defective requests are each REFUSED with their exact stop condition — targeting main, absent credential, a request carrying a credential value, an unbounded budget, a dirty worktree, a deployment scope, an item the board did not select, and a checkout drifted from the authorized SHA — each also asserted to route the program to BLOCKED and to authorize nothing; (d) a board with a drifted production-deploy authorization is refused; (e) the live preflight decision on real PR state is printed for the record without asserting its verdict, because the board's state legitimately changes and a gate must not depend on it.

Found by dry-running the attestation locally before pushing it, which is why it was dry-run: the drifted-policy case asserted stop_condition === POLICY_AUTHORIZATION_DRIFT and got BOARD_INVALID. Both are correct — the committed schema pins production_deploy_authorized with `const: false` AND the policy invariants check it independently, so the drift trips two layers and the first-reported condition is the schema one. The assertion now requires both to appear rather than requiring the policy layer to be first. A speculative push would have turned this into a red CI run.

Transition recorded: RUNNING_WRITER -> WRITER_DONE after the bounded repair passed focused verification: node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs -> 126 pass, 0 fail (was 121; +5 for the repair, none deleted or relaxed); node control-plane/kernel.mjs check -> ok=true, violation_count=0; the workflow parses as valid YAML with two jobs, correct triggers and correct permission blocks.

CLOUD ATTESTATION OBTAINED — the ACP-002 runner harness is executable entirely in GitHub Actions, with no dependency on any local machine. Control Plane Writer run 31956005284 on SHA 437a119b2978972f54992c85ab7e60c7b929e2b7: job `attest` 95186636816 SUCCESS, job `writer` 95186637210 SKIPPED. Every attestation step passed on the runner: 'The harness itself runs here, not on anybody's laptop' (node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs and node control-plane/kernel.mjs check executed on the GitHub runner), 'The preflight refuses a bad request — fail closed, proved in the cloud', 'This job holds no write scope, and says so from the file itself', and 'Record the live preflight decision on real PR state'. The steps are hard assertions, so SUCCESS means each of the eight defective requests was refused with its exact stop condition and each was proved to route the program to BLOCKED and authorize nothing.

The writer job was SKIPPED on that pull_request event, proving the `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` gate holds: attesting the runner did not run a writer, spend a provider credential, or push anything.

Live preflight decision recorded in the cloud on real PR state (informational, not asserted): ok=false, stop_condition=ITEM_NOT_AUTHORIZED, failed_condition_count=2 — condition 2 because deterministic selection said ADVANCE_IN_FLIGHT rather than RUN_WRITER while ACP-002 was itself WRITER_DONE, and condition 7 because the attestation job holds no provider credential by design. Conditions 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 all reported ok=true against real state. That is the fail-closed path exercised on the live board, in Actions.

REQUIRED CI OBTAINED ON THE REPAIRED SHA: CI run 31956005227 on 437a119b2978972f54992c85ab7e60c7b929e2b7 completed SUCCESS across all five required jobs — clinical-safety 95186636546, aislamiento-tenant 95186636562, lint (trinquete) 95186636591, verificar 95186636606, e2e-publico 95186636674. The ACP-001 bootstrap run 31956005203 concluded 'skipped' again; no writer fired.
Transition recorded: WRITER_DONE -> CI_PENDING on the repaired candidate.

Transition recorded: CI_PENDING -> SHA_FROZEN. FROZEN_CANDIDATE_SHA=437a119b2978972f54992c85ab7e60c7b929e2b7 — the immutable ACP-002 candidate selected for independent audit. It is the exact object that passed both the required CI and the cloud attestation. Every mandatory ACP-002 gate passed before the freeze, so this is not a candidate known to be defective: the dispatchability blocker that stopped the previous freeze is repaired and proved repaired in Actions.
The freeze does not skip the judge: SHA_FROZEN -> JUDGE_PASS is rejected with SKIPPED_STATE, so closure still has to pass through RUNNING_JUDGE and an independent verdict.
Transition recorded: SHA_FROZEN -> RUNNING_JUDGE. One independent read-only Codex audit is authorized against frozen SHA 437a119b2978972f54992c85ab7e60c7b929e2b7.

.github/workflows/control-plane-acp002-judge.yml added as ORCHESTRATION, not as part of the candidate. It is committed after the freeze on purpose, exactly as the ACP-001 judge was (commit 06cb256f followed freeze 09ca7c51): the auditor's harness must never be part of the artefact under audit, so the frozen tree does not contain it and the judge checks that tree out from outside.

This is NOT ACP-003. ACP-003 is a generalised, reusable judge runner; this is a one-off judge pinned to a single immutable SHA, the same shape ACP-001 used. ACP-003 remains QUEUED and the judge workflow asserts that as a precondition, exiting 85 if ACP-003 has moved.

Judge governance: permissions contents:read, actions:read, pull-requests:read; openai/codex-action with permission-profile ':read-only' and safety-strategy drop-sudo; the candidate checkout carries persist-credentials:false so nothing in the audit can push; the run fails closed with MISSING_REQUIRED_SECRET_OR_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIAL if OPENAI_API_KEY is absent; the structured verdict is validated with jq for audited_sha == the frozen SHA, independent == true, read_only == true and a verdict within {PASS, FAIL, UNVERIFIABLE}; and the orchestration head is proved not to have moved during the audit.

Fourteen mandatory gates are put to the judge, derived from what ACP-002 actually claims: preflight_conditions_complete, fail_closed_on_every_condition, least_privilege_writer, no_production_reach, no_main_merge_path, credential_never_read, bounded_budget, single_writer_lock, board_driven_selection, cloud_executable_attestation, attestation_is_read_only, reverse_mutation_proof, no_acp003_scope_leak, focused_tests. UNVERIFIABLE may never be reported as PASS.

Independent Codex judge run 31956327110 job 95187412888 completed with conclusion SUCCESS; contents:read, permission-profile ':read-only', drop-sudo, persist-credentials:false on the candidate checkout. Orchestration head proved stable: start == end == 2c6fcb9486a28179051398aff416da0d3f3d6a53, so SHA_CHANGED_DURING_AUDIT did not occur.

Structured Codex verdict on frozen SHA 437a119b2978972f54992c85ab7e60c7b929e2b7: FAIL. Preconditions verified before any transition: audited_sha matches the frozen candidate, independent == true, read_only == true, verdict within the allowed enum. Verbatim verdict preserved in control-plane/verdicts/acp002-codex-verdict-31956327110.json (artifact acp002-codex-verdict-31956327110, id 9266088312, zip sha256 545634257262e9d34fe8994d2dd2ba77b6d527a8ef5f989cfa04ac1c72fdd052, GitHub retention ends 2026-09-15).

Gates PASS: least_privilege_writer, single_writer_lock, cloud_executable_attestation, attestation_is_read_only, no_acp003_scope_leak. Gates FAIL: preflight_conditions_complete, fail_closed_on_every_condition, no_production_reach, no_main_merge_path, credential_never_read, bounded_budget, board_driven_selection, reverse_mutation_proof. Gate UNVERIFIABLE: focused_tests.

focused_tests came back UNVERIFIABLE because the judge's read-only sandbox rejected the suite's temporary mutant files with EROFS. That is a defect in how the mutation tests are built, not in the judge: loadMutant writes to os.tmpdir(), so the suite cannot be independently re-run by any read-only auditor. A proof an auditor cannot execute is not a proof. UNVERIFIABLE is not PASS and is treated as a gate failure.

Six blocking P1 findings recorded verbatim in the verdict file. Four were reproduced locally against the frozen code before being accepted, rather than taken on the judge's word: (a) permissions={} is AUTHORIZED by condition 9, because the validation loop over an empty object body never executes; (b) a credential value nested under an object such as {creds:{api_key}} is not seen, since the leak scan only inspects top-level keys; (c) a top-level field named `token` is not seen either, because the regex requires an underscore-prefixed suffix; (d) WRITER_MAX_RETRIES is placed in the request but never compared against GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT, so a re-run re-invokes the writer despite max_retries=0. The remaining two are plain readings of the committed code and are accepted: the writer checkout keeps its contents:write credential while the writer holds Bash(node|npm|npx), which can reach git through a child process before the scope and branch checks run; and the post-write allowlist only proves paths are under control-plane/, so a writer authorized for one item may edit another item's records.

The reverse-proof finding is accepted and is the most uncomfortable one, because it is about the tests I wrote to prove the thing works: the condition 1, 3 and 6 mutants flip their own check to true while overall ok stays false and authorized stays null, since another condition still fails. The tests assert only the individual check, so a test named 'without condition 1, an invalid board would start a writer' does not actually demonstrate that. The claim outran the assertion.

Transition recorded: RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_FAIL. statusForJudgeVerdict('FAIL') maps to JUDGE_FAIL, and the kernel refuses RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_PASS on this verdict with JUDGE_PASS_CONTRADICTS_VERDICT, so the FAIL could not have been quietly promoted.

Transition recorded: JUDGE_FAIL -> REPAIR_READY. Legal because six findings are severity P1 and blocking; the same transition offered only P2/P3 findings is refused with P2_P3_AUTO_REPAIR_FORBIDDEN, so the repair loop was opened by demonstrated blockers and not by policy drift.
NOT frozen, NOT closed, and ACP-003 untouched. The 437a119 candidate stands rejected; a repaired candidate must earn a newly frozen SHA and a fresh independent audit.

OWNER INTERVENTION RECONCILED, not overwritten. While this session held the writer, the owner pushed two commits to the branch: cc78bd2 preserving the Codex FAIL artifact, and 16f0e7c adding .github/workflows/acp002-owner-emergency-repair.yml, an owner-authorized one-shot cloud repair. Both are kept. The owner's verdict file is a superset of the one written here — same verdict, plus artifact_id 9266088312 and artifact_digest sha256:545634257262e9d34fe8994d2dd2ba77b6d527a8ef5f989cfa04ac1c72fdd052 — so the owner's copy was kept byte-for-byte and this session's duplicate was discarded on rebase.

The owner's cloud repair RAN AND FAILED: ACP-002 Owner Emergency Repair run 31957444430 job 95190110127, step 'Run one owner-authorized bounded Claude repair'. The writer worked for 27 minutes over 28 turns and then terminated on Anthropic API 400 'Credit balance is too low' (terminal_reason=api_error, total_cost_usd 7.636). The scope check, verification, and commit/push steps were all SKIPPED, so nothing was written and nothing was pushed. No repaired candidate exists from that run.

One writer was preserved throughout: the cloud repair is dead, no writer job is running, and this session is the single writer. Advancing ACP-002 to REPAIR_READY is also the interlock — the owner's emergency workflow asserts `ACP-002 must start RUNNING_JUDGE` and will now fail closed at its own precondition if it re-fires, so it cannot become a second writer behind this one's back. That workflow is deliberately left in place rather than deleted; it is the owner's, and its precondition is what makes it safe.

BLOCKED ON BILLING, DECLARED: the cloud writer path cannot be re-run until the Anthropic credit balance is restored. That is a spending decision reserved to the owner and was not touched. The repair itself does not depend on it — this session is the writer and can perform the bounded repair directly.

Transition recorded: REPAIR_READY -> RUNNING_WRITER; writer lock granted to run session-repair-p1x6 for ACP-002, and the same transition without the lock is refused with WRITER_LOCK_NOT_HELD. Marked before the repair is written.

REPAIR DELIVERED for all six blocking P1s. Files changed: control-plane/preflight.mjs, control-plane/preflight.test.mjs, control-plane/scope-guard.mjs (new), control-plane/scope-guard.test.mjs (new), control-plane/item-scopes.json (new), control-plane/kernel.test.mjs, .github/workflows/control-plane-writer.yml, and this board. control-plane/kernel.mjs and control-plane/MASTER_BOARD.schema.json were NOT touched — the ACP-001 artefact Codex already passed stays byte-identical.

P1-1 fixed (hostile input). Three real holes, each reproduced before being fixed: `permissions: {}` was AUTHORIZED because the validation loop had nothing to iterate and an empty failure list reads as success — an empty block now refuses, and so does one that never mentions `contents`; the credential scan only looked at top-level keys, so `{creds:{api_key}}` was invisible — it now walks the whole request recursively, tolerates cycles, and bounds depth; the key pattern required an underscore-prefixed suffix, so a plain `token` walked through — it now matches the word anywhere in the key and also flags credential-SHAPED values under innocent keys. One narrow exemption, declared: a value that is exactly none|read|write|admin is a GitHub permission level, not a secret, because the scope literally named `id-token` would otherwise flag itself.

P1-1 fixed (CLI contract). Every CLI exit now emits the full machine contract. The no-argument path used to return a bespoke {ok,error,usage} with no `authorized`, no `next_board_status` and no `stop_condition`, so a caller checking 'was anything authorized?' read undefined — and undefined is not a refusal.

P1-2 fixed (fence bypass). The writer checkout is now `persist-credentials: false`, so no reusable git credential sits in the working tree while the writer runs; the writer's tools are Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep with `--disallowedTools "Bash"` — the old Bash(node|npm|npx) allowance was decorative, since node can spawn git and npx can run arbitrary scripts; and the GitHub token exists only inside the final push step, passed per-invocation with `git -c http.extraheader` so it is never written into .git/config, after the preflight, the writer, the scope guard and the focused verification have all passed.

P1-3 fixed (item scope). New control-plane/item-scopes.json declares per-item write scope, and new control-plane/scope-guard.mjs enforces it: every changed path must be in the authorized item's declared list, only that item's board record may differ, all other items and every top-level governance field must be canonically identical before and after, and the item may not rewrite its own id, title, owner or dependencies. An item with no declared scope has no scope and cannot run — absence is a refusal, not a wildcard. The board snapshot is taken before the writer starts and kept outside the working tree, so the writer cannot edit its own baseline.

P1-4 fixed (retry ceiling). The request now carries the real GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT and condition 8 spends the ceiling against it: attempt N is legal only while N <= max_retries + 1. With max_retries 0, attempt 2 refuses before the Claude CLI is installed. An undeclared, zero, negative, fractional or string attempt refuses too.

P1-5 fixed (cosmetic condition 11). The condition used to read one boolean off the board — the board agreeing with itself. It now parses the committed judge workflows and checks their real permission blocks, refusing any write scope and requiring contents to be read or none. No workflow supplied, an unparseable one, or a missing job all fail closed. A test pins the real committed ACP-002 judge workflow at {contents:read, actions:read, pull-requests:read}.

P1-6 fixed (proofs that did not prove). The judge was right and this was the uncomfortable one. Reverse proofs now assert the mutant AUTHORIZES A WRITER — result.ok === true and a non-null `authorized` — via assertMutantAuthorizes, with assertRealPreflightRefuses pinning the committed behaviour on the same input. Where a single mutation genuinely cannot authorize because a second layer stands behind it (conditions 1, 3 and 6 are each backed by deterministic selection or by the committed schema), that fact is now ASSERTED as its own test and a second test removes every layer and shows the writer being authorized. The tests no longer claim more than they demonstrate.

P1-6b fixed (UNVERIFIABLE gate). Mutants are no longer written to os.tmpdir(); they are imported from data: URLs, so the suite touches no filesystem and a read-only auditor can reproduce every proof. That applies to preflight.test.mjs, scope-guard.test.mjs and kernel.test.mjs. Two lines of the kernel COPY are rewritten in memory because kernel.mjs resolves its own directory from import.meta.url, which has no file path under a data: URL; the committed kernel is untouched and no assertion changed.

Two defects in the repair were caught by dry-running it rather than by pushing it: the new credential scan flagged the GitHub permission scope `id-token: none` as a leaked secret, and the data: URL mutants tripped kernel.mjs's own top-level fileURLToPath. Both fixed before anything left this machine.

Verification: node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs -> 160 pass, 0 fail (was 126; +34 for this repair, none deleted or relaxed). node control-plane/kernel.mjs check -> ok=true, violation_count=0. node control-plane/scope-guard.mjs CLI -> exit 0 on a clean write. The writer workflow parses as valid YAML with the writer job gated to workflow_dispatch at contents:write and the attest job gated to pull_request at contents:read.

Scope note, declared rather than buried: control-plane/kernel.test.mjs is in ACP-002's declared scope solely for the P1-6b mechanism change. Only the mutant loader changed; no assertion, guard or expected violation code was altered, and kernel.mjs stays out of scope entirely.

Transition recorded: RUNNING_WRITER -> WRITER_DONE. JUDGE_PASS and CLOSED remain unclaimed. The rejected 437a119 candidate is not revived: a repaired candidate must earn required CI, a fresh cloud attestation, a NEW frozen SHA and a fresh independent audit.

Attestation caught up with the repair, and it caught it the honest way — by failing. Control Plane Writer run 31959714663 job 95195721275 FAILED at 'The preflight refuses a bad request', because the attestation's own control request predated the repair and no longer carried the newly required run_attempt and judge_workflows, so the control assertion 'the committed writer permissions must pass' was correctly false. The attestation was doing its job: it refused to certify a runner it could not satisfy.

The attestation now supplies both new fields and covers the repair itself. Eight further defective requests are refused in the cloud with their exact stop conditions — empty permissions block, permissions never mentioning contents, credential nested inside an object, credential under a short key name, re-run beyond the retry ceiling, undeclared run attempt, judge workflow granting write, and no judge workflow to inspect — bringing the cloud-attested refusals to sixteen. Two scope-guard refusals were added as well: an ACP-002 writer modifying ACP-003 (FOREIGN_ITEM_MODIFIED) and an item with no declared scope (NO_DECLARED_SCOPE).

The whole attestation script was extracted from the workflow and executed locally before pushing, exactly as with the previous round; all sixteen refusals, the two-layer drift case and both scope-guard cases pass. That habit has now caught four defects before they reached CI.

The owner's emergency repair workflow behaved as the interlock predicted: run 31959714684 stopped at 'Verify immutable FAIL evidence and canonical repair preconditions' because ACP-002 is no longer RUNNING_JUDGE. The Claude CLI was never installed and the writer was never invoked, so no credit was spent and no second writer existed.

OWNER INTERVENTION RECONCILED AGAIN, not overwritten: the owner pushed 3afcc6b and 4a2e6ec adding .github/workflows/acp002-attestation-fix.yml, a bounded cloud writer aimed at the same attestation fixture this session had already repaired locally. Both commits are kept and both owner workflows remain in the tree. Their runs pushed nothing, so no work of theirs was lost or duplicated.

Their runs did establish two facts worth more than the fix itself. First, the Anthropic credit balance is restored: run 31961047393 completed 'Install Claude Code CLI', 'Run one bounded Claude harness repair', the scope check and the focused verification, all successfully. Second, and this is the finding: it then died at the push with GitHub's own refusal — 'refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/control-plane-writer.yml without `workflows` permission'.

PLATFORM CONSTRAINT ADOPTED AS A GUARD. GITHUB_TOKEN can never push a change to .github/workflows/**. The repaired writer push step staged exactly that file and ACP-002's declared scope granted it, so this runner had the same latent defect: a writer could pass the preflight, spend its whole budget, satisfy the scope guard and the tests, and only then be refused by the server. That is the worst place to say no. So the refusal moved to the front — scope-guard.mjs now rejects any changed path under .github/ with WORKFLOW_PATH_UNPUSHABLE, rejects any item scope that DECLARES such a path, ACP-002's scope no longer contains one, and the push step stages only control-plane/. Four tests plus a reverse proof cover it, including one asserting that no committed scope declares an unpushable path.

This strengthens P1-2 rather than merely working around the error: 'a writer cannot edit its own runner' is now enforced by GitHub itself, with our allowlist agreeing with the platform instead of promising something the platform will refuse.

Verification after this change: node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs -> 164 pass, 0 fail (was 160). node control-plane/kernel.mjs check -> ok=true. The writer workflow still parses with the writer job at contents:write gated to workflow_dispatch and the attest job at contents:read gated to pull_request.

REPAIRED CANDIDATE CLOUD GATES: CI run 31963015797 completed SUCCESS on exact SHA 821a44b0da15959041e4af22990b2bcd499a59a7; Control Plane Writer attestation run 31963015715 completed SUCCESS on the same SHA.
Transition recorded: WRITER_DONE -> CI_PENDING after required CI and PR attestation both passed on exact repaired SHA 821a44b0da15959041e4af22990b2bcd499a59a7.

FROZEN_CANDIDATE_SHA=821a44b0da15959041e4af22990b2bcd499a59a7; immutable repaired ACP-002 candidate selected for fresh independent Codex re-audit. The previously rejected 437a119b2978972f54992c85ab7e60c7b929e2b7 candidate remains rejected and is not reused.
Transition recorded: CI_PENDING -> SHA_FROZEN after exact-SHA cloud gates passed.

Transition recorded: SHA_FROZEN -> RUNNING_JUDGE; one fresh independent read-only Codex audit is authorized against 821a44b0da15959041e4af22990b2bcd499a59a7. ACP-003 remains QUEUED; no merge, deploy, PHI, clinical-policy change, secret rotation, or destructive action is authorized.

Second independent Codex audit: run 31963800078 job 95205728114, conclusion SUCCESS, contents:read + ':read-only' + drop-sudo, orchestration head proved stable at c911260630ffe28c22a186b8057d65cb71a4f4e4. Structured verdict on frozen SHA 821a44b0da15959041e4af22990b2bcd499a59a7: FAIL. Verbatim verdict in control-plane/verdicts/acp002-codex-verdict-31963800078.json (artifact 9268002438, sha256 f462731274d32eea7e4d86f976f77a67a5e5a570a8d23d61a68b23493352cfbd).

Progress that is real: focused_tests moved from UNVERIFIABLE to a partial run — the judge executed the preflight and scope-guard suites and node control-plane/kernel.mjs check (ok=true) inside its read-only sandbox, which the previous audit could not do at all. The remaining blocker there is now P2 and different in kind: kernel.test.mjs's CLI test uses execFileSync to spawn Node and the sandbox denies it with EPERM. The data: URL fix removed the EROFS wall; a child-process restriction is behind it.

SEVEN BLOCKING P1s, and five of them are holes this session introduced while repairing the previous six. Recorded plainly: (1) the credential scan's own depth cap of 8 became the bypass — a secret at ten levels is authorized; (2) writerPermissionsFromWorkflow does not stop at the next job, so deleting the writer's permissions block makes it read the attest job's and authorize anyway; (3) GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT only counts re-runs of one run, so a fresh workflow_dispatch restarts at attempt 1 and max_retries:0 bounds nothing durable; (4) ACP-002's declared scope contains scope-guard.mjs and item-scopes.json while the guard is executed from the working tree AFTER the writer, so a writer can weaken the very guard that will judge it and then edit ACP-003; (5) the scope check reads git-status paths and never inspects .git/config, so a writer holding Write/Edit can install a URL rewrite and redirect the later token-bearing push.
Finding 4 is the sharpest of the set and deserves naming: the guard that enforces item scope was itself inside the scope it enforces. A check a writer can edit before the check runs is not a check.

Finding 6 is a second pass over the same lesson as the first audit's P1-6: condition 5 has no removal proof at all, and the condition-2 proof still asserts only that its own check flipped rather than that a writer would be authorized. The standard was stated for the suite and then not applied uniformly.

Finding 7 is a process defect in the freeze, not in the code: 821a44b DID pass CI run 31963015797 and attestation run 31963015715, but that evidence was written in commit 69d58a9, which comes AFTER the frozen SHA. The immutable candidate therefore contains a board still saying the attestation FAILED and still demanding CI before a freeze. A candidate must carry its own green evidence at the SHA being judged; recording it in a later commit does not reach the auditor. Future freezes must land the evidence first and freeze the commit that contains it.
Transition recorded: RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_FAIL on the structured FAIL verdict; the kernel refuses RUNNING_JUDGE -> JUDGE_PASS on this verdict with JUDGE_PASS_CONTRADICTS_VERDICT.
Transition recorded: JUDGE_FAIL -> REPAIR_READY; seven findings are P1 and blocking, so the repair loop is opened by demonstrated blockers. The single P2 could not have opened it.
821a44b is now REJECTED alongside 437a119. Neither is revived. ACP-003 remains QUEUED; no merge, no deploy, no PHI, no production credential.
Transition recorded: REPAIR_READY -> RUNNING_WRITER for checkpointed cloud repair run 31992739956. Owner authorized continuing the bounded P1 repair; ACP-003 remains QUEUED.
